title: Protocol to Study the Immune Profile of Syngeneic Mouse Tumor Models
author: Miyauchi, Arimoto, et al.
materials: Countess II FL automated cell counter

The staining panels for flow cytometry in this protocol were designed for NovoCyte Advanteon Flow Cytometer (Agilent Technologies) equipped with 3 lasers (violet, blue, and red) and a total of 19 detectors. Staining panels need to be designed based on the configuration of your flow cytometer and your proteins/markers of interest.Note: Examples of staining panels for myeloid cells and lymphoid cells are shown in Table 1 and Table 2, respectively.4.Know the configuration of your flow cytometer: number of lasers, number of detectors, and range of wavelengths.5.Design your staining panel.a.Use brighter fluorochromes for rare/lowly expressed proteins and use dimmer fluorochromes for highly expressed proteins.b.If possible, use different lasers for markers of the same cell population. For example, Treg markers CD25 and Foxp3 are best detected using fluorochromes excited by different lasers. steps.title: Prepare cell cultures for injection
steps.instruction: Revive frozen B16F10, LLC, or MC38 cells in the appropriate medium, passage at least once (use passages 2–3), and grow to ~80 % confluency before harvesting for injection.

steps.title: Prepare surface antibody master mix
steps.instruction: Create a 2× antibody master mix in flow cytometry buffer using the dilutions listed in Table 1 (myeloid) and Table 2 (lymphoid). Each antibody is added at the specified dilution (e.g., Zombie Aqua 1:1000, CD45.2 1:104, CD11b 1:200, etc.) and the appropriate catalog number.

steps.title: Prepare intracellular antibody master mix
steps.instruction: Create an antibody master mix in 1× permeabilization buffer using the same antibodies as above (or a subset) at the dilutions listed, for intracellular staining.

substeps.instruction: Use the same dilution factors as in the surface panel for each intracellular‑targeted antibody (e.g., Foxp3 1:100).
Prepare the mix in 1× permeabilization buffer.

steps.title: Plate cells for staining
steps.instruction: Dispense 1 × 10⁶ cells into each well of a v‑bottom 96‑well plate (maximum volume 350 µL per well).

steps.title: Wash cells with PBS
steps.instruction: Add PBS up to 200 µL per well, centrifuge 400–600 × g for 3–5 min at 20–25 °C, discard supernatant by flipping the plate.

steps.title: Live/Dead staining
steps.instruction: Resuspend cells in 100 µL per well of Live/Dead staining solution, incubate 15 min at 20–25 °C (or 30 min on ice) in the dark.

steps.title: Wash after Live/Dead
steps.instruction: Wash cells twice with PBS: add 100 µL PBS, centrifuge 400–600 × g for 3–5 min at 20–25 °C, discard supernatant, then resuspend in 200 µL PBS and repeat.

steps.title: Surface antibody staining
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of the 2× surface antibody master mix to each well (final volume 100 µL), incubate 30 min on ice in the dark.

steps.title: Wash after surface staining
steps.instruction: Wash cells twice with flow cytometry buffer: add 100 µL buffer, centrifuge 400–600 × g for 3–5 min at 20–25 °C, discard supernatant, resuspend in 200 µL buffer, repeat.

steps.title: Intracellular antibody staining
steps.instruction: Resuspend cells in 100 µL of intracellular antibody master mix, incubate 30 min at 20–25 °C in the dark.

steps.title: Wash after intracellular staining
steps.instruction: Wash cells twice with 1× permeabilization buffer: add 100 µL buffer, centrifuge 800–1,000 × g for 3–5 min at 20–25 °C, discard supernatant, resuspend in 200 µL buffer, repeat.

steps.title: Final resuspension
steps.instruction: Resuspend stained cells in 150–200 µL flow cytometry buffer (or appropriate volume for acquisition).

steps.title: Prepare FMO control samples
steps.instruction: For each fluorochrome, repeat the staining workflow but omit the corresponding antibody at the surface staining step (Step 38) or intracellular staining step (Step 49) to generate fluorescence‑minus‑one controls.

steps.title: Prepare compensation beads
steps.instruction: Follow the manufacturers’ protocols to stain UltraComp eBeads Plus with each fluorescent‑conjugated antibody and to stain ArC Amine Reactive Compensation Beads with amine‑reactive viability dyes.

steps.title: Store fixed samples
steps.instruction: Keep fixed samples at 4 °C; acquire data within 3 days (note that some tandem dyes may degrade faster).

description: This protocol describes processes in investigating anti-tumor immune response by analyzing immune cell profiles in syngeneic mouse tumor models. Here, we analyzed B16F10 melanoma, LLC lung carcinoma, and MC38 colon carcinoma in C57BL/6 mice. However, this protocol could be applied broadly to tumor types to obtain single-cell preparations by optimizing the tissue dissociation step. We have also used this protocol for E0771 mammary cancer in C57BL/6 mice and 4T1 mammary cancer in BALB/c mice. The staining panels for flow cytometry analysis can be modified depending on the immune populations of interest or the flow cytometer configuration.
